thread.title: Facebook is in bear market territory, Apple is in a correction, and they are far from alone - MarketWatch

author: Wallace Witkowski
title: Facebook is in bear market territory, Apple is in a correction, and they are far from alone - MarketWatch
text:
After the worst quarter for stocks in more than two years and another decline at the beginning of a new quarter Monday, nearly a fifth of the S&P 500’s tech sector has slipped into bear territory, led by Facebook Inc.’s decline of more than 20%.
About 70% of the sector, including Apple Inc. AAPL, -1.07% is in correction territory, with big names like Microsoft Corp. MSFT, -3.54% flirting with correction levels. Some big tech companies, like Google parent Alphabet Inc. GOOG, -2.97% GOOGL, -2.97% are already there and approaching bear levels.
Read more about bear markets and corrections
A bear market is defined as 20% or more off the stock’s 52-week high, while a correction is 10% or more off the 52-week high. Tech stocks have an increasingly large effect on stock indexes because of their weighting: The sector accounts for $6.473 trillion, or about 28%, of the S&P 500’s $23.438 trillion in market cap spread across 11 sectors, according to FactSet data.
On Monday, 13 out of the tech 69 stocks on the S&P 500 index SPX, -2.75% were 20% or more off their 52-week high, or at bear levels.

Large-cap tech companies—those worth $100 billon or more—that are already in correction territory include Apple, Alphabet, Cisco Systems Inc. CSCO, -4.60% International Business Machines Corp. IBM, -2.69% , Nvidia Corp. NVDA, -5.08% Intel Corp. INTC, -6.41% and Oracle Corp. ORCL, -2.17%
Shares of Microsoft and Adobe Systems Inc. ADBE, -2.45% are flirting with entering correction territory, with both stocks more than 9% off their 52-week highs.
